_comment: The accredited-diploma credit contract: how much XP is a credit, how many
credits each subject needs, and what an official transcript calls it.
One definition because it was five. web/src/utils/creditRequirements.js held
the requirement table; services/credit_mapping_service.py held a second copy
under a comment reading 'Aligned with web/src/utils/creditRequirements.js',
which is a request that a person do a job a test should do. XP_PER_CREDIT
was written out in five backend modules and once on the web. The formal
transcript names were in three backend modules and the web table.
The web test that guards this (studentContextCredits.test.jsx) records what
the drift cost last time: two copies said Social Studies was 3.5 against the
4.0 the other two said, and because two of them were never read, nothing
caught it.
transcriptName is the LONG form on purpose -- 'Mathematics', not 'Math'.
shared/data/subjects.json carries the short names the pickers show, and its
comment explains why the two lists differ. This is the transcript's
vocabulary; that one is the picker's.
Order follows subjects.json, which is transcript order.
NOT here, because it is not the standard diploma: backend/utils/oea_pathways.py
defines alternative graduation pathways with their own per-subject credit
counts. Those are a different product, not a second copy of this one.
